description:
The F_7 receipt campaign (6c7fcb38) records launch-time dynamic shared-memory allocation as a measurement blind spot: rocprofv3's counter collection reports LDS_Block_Size 0 (static LDS only) for kernels whose dynamic allocation the design predicts (24n bytes for wave_gf7_three_plane_kernel, 8n*ceil(n/16) for the shared-table kernels). A rocprofv2 capability probe committed at dev/studies/6c7fcb38/profiled-20260815T181923Z/rocprofv2-n20-threeplane/ captured LDS_Per_Workgroup 512 for the walk kernel at n=20 in its four pre-crash dispatches — the design's 480-byte prediction at 128-byte allocation granularity — indicating rocprofv2 reports the launch-time dynamic figure rocprofv3 does not. rocprofv2 aborts this workload under full interception (recorded in the same artifact's run2.log), so a usable pass needs a workaround (e.g. minimal counter set, per-kernel filtering, or tolerating the abort after enough dispatches).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A committed evidence pass records the launch-time dynamic LDS allocation for every executing F_7 device kernel with a design-stated shared-memory budget, over the hash-pinned campaign binary, compared against the design predictions at the allocator's granularity; kernels the tooling cannot capture are recorded as such with the failing command.
- [hard] REQ-02: The receipts' shared-memory blind-spot statements (dev/studies/6c7fcb38/receipts.md sections 7.1, 8, 17) are updated to cite the new evidence, and every claim remains reproducible from committed artifacts.
title: Dynamic LDS confirmation pass for F_7 device kernels via rocprofv2
